item.title: Forest Value
item.description:
Forest Value

Evaluating the environmental, ecological, and social value of forests.

Overview
#

Forests provide many forms of value beyond timber production.

They support biodiversity, store carbon, regulate water, protect landscapes, and contribute to human well-being. Our laboratory evaluates these values from ecological, environmental, economic, and social perspectives.

Research Questions
#

  • How can the multiple values of forests be measured and visualized?
  • How do forest conditions influence ecosystem services?
  • How can forest value be reflected in management and policy decisions?
  • How do people perceive and use forest?

Research Topics
#

  • Ecosystem services
  • Biodiversity assessment
  • Carbon sequestration
  • Landscape evaluation
  • Sustainable forest management
  • Social and cultural value of forests

Methods
#

We combine field surveys, spatial analysis, environmental assessment, and social surveys to evaluate forest value from multiple perspectives.

item.title: Wood Utilization
item.description:
Wood Utilization

Assessing the environmental performance and climate benefits of wood utilization.

Overview
#

Wood utilization can contribute to climate change mitigation, regional industries, and sustainable forest management.

Our laboratory evaluates the environmental impacts and benefits of wood products throughout their life cycles, from forest management and harvesting to manufacturing, use, recycling, and disposal.

Research Questions
#

  • What are the greenhouse gas emissions associated with wood products?
  • How much carbon is stored in long-lived wood products?
  • Under what conditions does wood substitution reduce environmental impacts?
  • How can local wood utilization support sustainable forest management?

Research Topics
#

  • Life Cycle Assessment
  • Greenhouse gas accounting
  • Carbon storage in wood products
  • Material and energy substitution
  • Local timber utilization
  • Circular use of wood resources

Methods
#

We use Life Cycle Assessment, carbon accounting, material flow analysis, and scenario analysis to evaluate the environmental performance of wood utilization.

item.title: Regional Economy
item.description:
Regional Economy

Evaluating the regional economic impacts of forestry and wood-based industries.

Overview
#

Forestry and wood utilization generate economic activity through harvesting, transportation, processing, construction, and related local industries.

Our laboratory studies how forest resources and wood-based industries contribute to regional employment, income, production, and economic circulation.

Research Questions
#

  • How much economic activity is generated by forestry and wood utilization?
  • Which industries benefit from increased local timber use?
  • How does local procurement affect the regional economy?
  • How can forest-related industries contribute to regional revitalization?

Research Topics
#

  • Regional economic ripple effects
  • Forestry and timber industries
  • Local procurement
  • Employment and income generation
  • Supply chains
  • Regional revitalization

Methods
#

We use input-output analysis, economic ripple-effect analysis, supply-chain analysis, statistical data, and interviews with local stakeholders.

item.title: Satoyama & Communities
item.description:
Satoyama & Communities

Exploring relationships between forests, biodiversity, culture, and local communities.

Overview
#

Satoyama landscapes have been shaped through long-term interactions between people and nature.

Changes in population, lifestyles, and forest use have weakened many of these relationships. Our laboratory studies ways to reconnect people with forests through biodiversity, local knowledge, forest products, cultural practices, and community activities.
